approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a persistent tree of molecular graph edits and buys newly reached frontier molecules directly. Accepted scores update exact completed-return and pending-count records along each purchased route. Similarity between eligible siblings shares peak values and exploration counts for selection, while widening still uses each route’s own counts. After a strict accepted incumbent improvement, it starts a fresh pair of roots from the new incumbent and the incumbent just replaced, using their original cached score receipts. All state stays inside the current objective session.
approach.novelty: Remove only borrowed completed and pending counts from exploration when choosing between the two promoted roots, while keeping their shared peak values. Each root then receives an exploration bonus based on its own completed and pending work. Earlier siblings removed shared values alone or shared values and counts together; later controls removed one count term under own values. This fills the missing joint-count comparison under shared values and tests whether that consumer helps or harms paid search.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 makes both fresh observed origins reachable but their coupled selection does not preserve useful refinement: complete Search mean 0.4809700595412967 (population SD 0.025313161830483537), paired loss 0.018526255130948004 against its single-root code Parent n-e4b751133c75, and full/late incumbent mass 4.08716922748481/0.8656010443094921. The limiting behavior addressed here is borrowed completed and pending counts suppressing promoted-root exploration while shared peak estimates remain active. Removing value alone in n-fc3b91c9623a gains 0.01917865290194668; removing value and both densities together in n-51af92d7316d gains 0.034092173748721186. Conversely, n-bf023e9ce9f8 and n-0fdf8aec31a2 lose 0.006156349369649307 and 0.04013074283123317 when individual densities are removed on the own-value host. These are conditional comparisons, not an additive estimate of the missing shared-value joint-density cell. Independent read-only replay of the Parent logs reproduces 613 changed choices among 3715 promoted-root decisions: own denominators increase all 7430 row bonuses, preserve B/D, and join to 581 actual Parent purchases, 298 late. Those joins show natural opportunity, not outcomes of the unrun alternative. See policy/scratch/r0059-03-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and its fifteen Search audits, which cite and hash underlying logs and trajectories. The pending-density literal-condition gap recorded in policy/scratch/search_policy-2a8260d5abcf/evidence-audit.json remains unresolved.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen Search Policy review and its recorded queries; no new query was issued. The Gelly-Silver primary PDF was opened directly and Sections 4.3-4.4 checked: its Go method keeps direct and shared action values distinct, blends them, and uses actual action counts for exploration. The present campaign retains molecular kernel peak sharing and pending batches; it tests the existing joint-density consumer while deliberately omitting RAVE action equivalence, blending and source guarantees. This is an internal control, so adoptions remain empty. The paper supports a conceptual distinction, not predicted molecular performance. New paid-path and endpoint evidence must answer the frozen question.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen intervention is an internal control of an existing consumer, supported by the exact missing factorial cell, archived selection rows and independently reproduced natural exposure. It introduces no source algorithm, value blend, action-equivalence claim, model or dependency. The changed joint exploration denominator is fully specified by existing route statistics and the frozen continuation.

hypothesis: Joint removal of off-diagonal completed and pending exploration density only at episode>0 and parent_id==0 on n-b13ef5ae4ba8. For eligible root i retain D_i=sum_j K_ij N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij O_j and B_i=sum_{j:N_j>0} K_ij N_j M_j as exact inherited shared rows, and retain exploitation V_i=B_i/D_i if D_i>0 else the inherited 0.5 default. Replace only exploration started_i=D_i+P_i by N_i+O_i, including the zero-start priority. The active index for positive started is V_i+0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(N_i+O_i)); resolve exact ties by earliest occurrence ID. D remains the value normalizer and is not overwritten by N. With nonnegative similarity and diagonal one, removing borrowed density weakly increases bonuses at fixed state, strictly when off-diagonal density is positive, and can change root choices and purchased descendants. This is an obstacle intervention on a different statistical consumer of the refuted membership Parent, not another membership-benefit prediction. The Child’s adaptive paid feedback determines its conditional endpoint sign.

finding_summary.headline: Exploration changed 743 paid routes; the mean gain barely clears the registered scale and remains far below the Anchor.
finding_summary.insights:
This completes the previously unobserved treatment cell without turning the small finite-panel gain into a reliability claim. Under the frozen shared-value composition, removing joint exploration density has a narrowly positive measured effect, so the retained joint consumer has a conditional negative contribution at the registered descriptive scale. Removing the same joint consumer under own values gains 0.01491352; the four-cell difference is +0.01282394, with seed differences spanning -0.04551 to +0.05727. That variation leaves generalization and separate completed-versus-pending attribution open. It does not repair the earlier pending-condition correspondence gap, reverse the membership finding or settle the route as a whole.

More switches did not mean consistently useful switched purchases: only 3 of the 743 changed-route purchases improved the incumbent. Preceding origins received 1,784 purchases versus 1,686 in the Parent, but their progress mass fell from 1.99807 to 0.69556 while current-origin progress increased. These are adaptive, selected strata and cannot establish mediation. The molecular evidence also shows a persistent proposal limitation: small-fragment purchases increased from 319 to 367, including 170 to 218 late, while the large-molecule tail stayed near 245. More than a thousand generic scaffolds remain represented, so wholesale scaffold collapse is unsupported. Useful ring, amine and polar arrangements are reachable, but graph edits do not preserve them reliably. A proposal operator that preserves useful local arrangements during scaffold and size changes, or a search scheme that ranks those alternatives using current-session feedback, could address that limitation; this experiment did not test either. No goal or approach completion is asserted.
finding_summary.results: The mechanism operated: all 7,510 exposed root rows received smaller exploration denominators and larger bonuses while retaining their shared peak values. It changed 785 root choices; 743 reached accepted paid purchases, including 468 late purchases. No isolation violation was detected. Across all three Search seeds, mean final score rose from 0.48097006 to 0.48305964, a gain of 0.00208958 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed differences were +0.04744, -0.05589 and +0.01472. Full incumbent progress rose from 4.08717 to 4.11851 and late progress from 0.86560 to 1.29429, while full strict improvements fell from 148 to 139. The formal Anchor remains ahead by 0.12397068; its performance target is unmet.

molecular.headline: Aromatic rings and amines coexist with tiny fragments, oversized fused graphs, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character:
Complete Child evaluation and complete paired comparison with the actual code Parent n-b13ef5ae4ba8 are distinct facts and both are available: frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, all covered objective sessions, 300 accepted records per session, ten initial and 290 optimizer records, batch ten. No requested trajectory or comparison path is missing. This assessment describes observed chemistry, without activation, ranking, component-contribution or mechanism judgments. The output spans fused heteroaromatics, substituted biaryls, ordinary amides/ethers and acyclic or ring-associated amines, alongside irregular bridged rings, hydrazines, N–O/O–O/N–halogen/O–halogen linkages and very small fragments. Formal parse acceptance does not establish synthesis, stability or biological usefulness; no routes or experimental chemistry were supplied. Drug-likeness is moderate as a qualitative whole-panel reading, with conventional medicinal motifs amid substantial liabilities.

Independent RDKit 2023.09.6 measurements of 4350 paid Child molecules show heavy-atom median 26, interquartile range 20–34, range 1–107; the Parent has median 26, interquartile range 20–34, range 1–117. Child below-six/above-fifty counts are 367/246, versus Parent 319/244. Late means paid ordinals 146 through 290 inclusive: 2175 records, with Child tails 218/144 versus Parent 170/141. Child ring-bearing/aromatic-ring-bearing counts are 3887/3536 versus Parent 3918/3365. Across the full panel, nonempty typed/generic Bemis–Murcko scaffold unions are 1770/1256 for the Child and 1837/1284 for the Parent; late unions are 1004/742 and 1042/776. Empty scaffolds remain counted separately: full Child/Parent 463/432, late 251/211. Broad graph/scaffold variety coexists with related high-score series; it does not prove broad useful chemistry.

For similarity only, exclude molecules with fewer than six heavy atoms. Use the same sparse-count Morgan radius-two fingerprints with chirality enabled and RDKit count Tanimoto (count intersection over union), forming unordered pairs within each objective session and pooling sums over pair counts, never cross-session pairs. Full Child mean 0.224225490 uses 527387 pairs from 3983 eligible molecules; Parent 0.222955539 uses 540155 pairs from 4031 molecules. Late Child 0.262881801 uses 127132 pairs from 1957 molecules; Parent 0.267514491 uses 133298 pairs from 2005 molecules. These descriptors are distinct from the selector's folded-count generalized dot-product Tanimoto and from earlier reports with different pooling. Original reports and corrections are preserved.

Descriptive log joins locate Child initial/current/preceding-origin paid counts at 770/1796/1784, with late counts 145/1011/1019; Parent counts are 770/1894/1686, late 145/1037/993. Child full origin heavy-atom medians are 26/26/26 and typed/generic scaffold unions are 319/236, 787/578 and 835/617. The Child's 743 paid records carrying an actual-choice changed-path flag have median 27 heavy atoms, tails 76/58, and typed/generic scaffold unions 367/287. Their within-session, within-stratum fragment-excluded similarity is 0.281866426 over 23061 pairs; 468 late flagged records have median 25, tails 67/33, unions 216/169 and similarity 0.290769510 over 9562 pairs. These are overlapping descriptive provenance strata, not a treatment-effect or activation assessment. The Parent lacks a directly matching historical changed-path flag for this Child intervention, so no zero-valued comparison is imputed.

Every paid Child string lacks tetrahedral stereochemical tokens; the independent nonlegacy RDKit chiral-centre audit identifies potential but unassigned centres in 2356 records. The same procedure gives 2570 for the Parent. These are newly defined descriptor readings (FindMolChiralCenters includeUnassigned=True, useLegacyImplementation=False), not a rewrite of historical stereocentre counts or the digest's text counters. All full/late, per-session and origin/flag-stratum details, exact source hashes and byte-identical in-run Child staging snapshots are in policy/scratch/r0059-03-improve-L01/molecular/evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit files. Explicit underlying Search trajectories/logs are cited per task. Snapshot copies preserve bytes but do not grant SMILES citation authority; cited molecules were separately checked against the frozen digest/trusted Child trajectories. Chemistry association is not component attribution; historical missing RNG/timing and trusted task-safety evidence remain unresolved outside this output assessment.

Preserve the original source and panel conditions; the observed association is not a component effect or demonstrated transfer benefit.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
